text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English/Australian poet and writer RICHARD HORNE was born in 1802.
Also born today in 1802 was HENRY JEANNERET, who wrote Australia's first book on "dentistry", called "Hints For The Preservation Of Teeth".

Australian conservative politician Sir BILLY MACKIE SNEDDEN was born on this day in 1926, and died under mysterious circumstances involving an unidentified blonde woman in a motel. Despite media speculation, the official verdict was death by natural causes.
JOHN (DOUG) ANTHONY was born in 1929, a farmer who went on to lead the conservative National (Country) Party.

British actor ANTHONY HOPKINS was born in 1937, and won an Oscar for his role in "Silence Of The Lambs". He played brutal mass murderer "Hannibal the Cannibal" and starred with JODIE FOSTER in the film. In 1994 he starred with EMMA THOMPSON in "The Remains of the Day".
British bassist with the Kinks, PETER QUAIFE, was born in 1943. He left the group in 1969 and was replaced by JOHN DALTON.

US singer, guitarist and songwriter JOHN DENVER (JOHN HENRY DEUTSCHENDORF) was born in 1943. He started his singing career as a member of the CHAD MITCHELL Trio in 1965. He composed "Leaving On A Jet Plane" for PETER, PAUL and MARY before his own singing career took off with a series of hits. These included "Take Me Home, Country Roads" (1971), "Sunshine On My Shoulders" (1974), "Annie's Song" (1974), "Back Home Again" (1974), "Thank God I'm A Country Boy" (1975) and "I'm Sorry/Calypso" (1975). All his hits were million sellers. In the eighties he recorded duets with artists including PLACIDO DOMINGO, SYLVIE VARTAN and EMMYLOU HARRIS.
Another British actor, BEN KINGSLEY was born in 1943, best-known for his performance as GANDHI in the film of the same name.

"The Queen of Disco" DONNA SUMMER was born in 1948. Her real name was LA DONNA ADRAIN GAINES. Hits included "Love To Love You Baby" (1975), "I Feel Love" (1977), "Love's Unkind" (1977), "Last Dance" (1978), "MacArthur Park" (1978), "She Works Hard For The Money" (1983), "This Time I Know It's For Real" (1989) and "I Don't Wanna Get Hurt" (1989).
US bassist with Aerosmith TOM HAMILTON was born in 1951.
** EVENTS **
1600 : Queen ELIZABETH I granted a charter to the
"company of merchants of London trading to the East Indies" - the East India Company.
1719 : Death of JOHN FLAMSTEED, the astronomer for whom
King CHARLES the Second built the Greenwich Observatory.
1922 : The French Government refused a German offer of a
non-aggression pact.
1948 : The KINSEY report into sexuality found that 56

percent of American men had been unfaithful to their wives. The "Sexual Behaviour of the Human Male" was written by Indiana University's professor ALFRED KINSEY. It was based on interviews with 5,300 men. Other findings were that 90 percent of American men masturbated and 37 percent had achieved orgasm with another man.
1953 : A British-led expedition to search for the

Abominable Snowman arrived in New Delhi. In June 1955 the team, led by CHARLES EVANS, conquered the highest unclimbed peak, Kanchenjunga, in India. However there was no evidence of the "yeti". The legendary creature, said to resemble a human, with long arms and thick hair covering the body, has been the subject of reported sightings since 1832. The reports of the Abominable Snowman's existence in the Himalayas gained substance in 1951 from a published photograph of a huge footprint in the snow.
1977 : The Cambodian Government broke off diplomatic ties
with Vietnam, and also suspended all air-services between the two countries.
1985 : American rock and country singer RICK NELSON, his
fiancee and four band members died when their chartered DC-3 crashed while flying to a concert in Texas.
1986 : Oil giant Exxon Corp cut all investment in South
Africa.
1990 : A Norwegian man was arrested for attacking the
giant 23-metre Christmas Tree in London's Trafalgar Square with a chainsaw.
1994 : Bosnia's Moslem-led government signed an agreement
for a four-month ceasefire in Bosnia, the 1,000th day of the bitter Serb siege of Sarajevo.
